---
title: "Dependency licenses"
---

wispack links three pieces of code whose licenses need to be read together: Rcpp (`GPL (>= 2)`), Stan Math's Intel TBB dependency (Apache License 2.0), and wispack's own code (`GPL (>= 3)`, see `LICENSE`). The Stan project's own licensing page states a real conflict here, but it's narrower than it sounds out of context, and it doesn't block this package.

**The conflict, as the Stan project states it:** Apache License 2.0 and GPL version 2 cannot be combined into a single distributed binary. The Free Software Foundation has never considered Apache 2.0 compatible with GPLv2, because Apache 2.0's patent-termination clause has no counterpart in GPLv2's text. See the [Stan wiki's Licensing page](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-Licensing) and the [FSF's license list](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.html) (entry for "Apache License 2.0").

**Why that doesn't block wispack:** GPLv3 was written specifically to fix this. Both the [FSF's license list](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.html) and the [Apache Software Foundation's own compatibility page](https://www.apache.org/licenses/GPL-compatibility) state that Apache 2.0 code can be combined with GPLv3 code and the combination distributed under GPLv3 (the reverse -- GPLv3 code going into an Apache-licensed project -- doesn't hold, but that's not the direction this package needs). Separately, Rcpp's own `License:` field is `GPL (>= 2)` -- "version 2 or any later version" -- so Rcpp itself permits being used and redistributed under GPLv3 terms, not only GPLv2.

Putting those together: wispack is licensed `GPL (>= 3)`, and distributing the combination of wispack + Rcpp + Stan Math + TBB as a whole under GPLv3 is exactly the case both the FSF and the ASF say is fine. This isn't a one-off argument specific to wispack, either -- it's the resolution the R/Stan ecosystem already relies on. `RcppParallel`, the CRAN package that actually ships the compiled TBB libraries wispack links against (via `StanHeaders`), is itself licensed `GPL (>= 3)` for this exact reason, and `rstan`/`brms`/`rstanarm` all ship CRAN binaries bundling Stan Math + TBB under the identical pattern. (The conflict would only be a real blocker for a package that was itself locked to GPLv2-only with no "or later" clause -- which is a choice, not something TBB or Stan Math force on a downstream package.)

<h1> Stan Math </h1>

Bob Carpenter  
https://bob-carpenter.github.io/

https://mc-stan.org/math/  
https://github.com/stan-dev/math

BSD 3-Clause License  

The Stan Math Library depends on the Intel TBB library (via `RcppParallel`), which is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license. This dependency implies an additional restriction as compared to the new BSD license alone: Apache 2.0 code can't be combined with GPLv2-only code in one distributed binary. See the explanation at the top of this page for why that doesn't affect wispack, which is licensed GPL (>= 3).
